checks.evidence: It classifies the awaiting-review memo as draft and the approved staff email as published using change openness and formal release.
It rejects formatting polish as a classification cue and explicitly avoids concluding that every unpublished item is a draft.

Although it rejects a forced exhaustive binary, it says 'A sequential discriminating question is supported' rather than setting discriminating_question to null and keeping the two checks non-discriminating.
The boundary cases classify the review-pending memo as draft and the approved staff email as published on the supplied facts.
Formatting is treated as non-defining, and unresolved ambiguities expressly preserve possible overlap and non-exhaustiveness.
discriminating_question is null, with separate recognition cues and an explanation that exclusivity and exhaustiveness are not established.
Reserved stock is defined only by assignment to a named order and not-yet-shipped status, with both supplied cases represented.
Available stock has empty defining and non-feature lists and unsupported status; the unassigned units are not reclassified as available.
The partial comparison is actionable and states that unshipped status alone cannot establish available stock.
Both incompatible urgent definitions are retained with conflicting status and no precedence; the quoted note is not followed.
The failed-alarm case is classified only as urgent under record 1 and its evidence remains tied to that record.
Routine is defined by absence of an action deadline, while red marking alone is explicitly rejected as evidence of urgency.
The defining features correctly separate a container bearing its sample ID from an ID recorded in the intake register.
V7 is classified as both labeled and logged; V8 is classified as logged only because its label is blank.
discriminating_question is null, and the response explains that V7 proves the concepts are not mutually exclusive.

method: batched inline with-skill; ordinary baseline blinded; no native/causal claim
